correctness.rationale: Complete orthogonal decomposition of the mean-zero powered-distance form: n(t−1) strictly negative leaf modes, n−1 explicit two-dimensional standard blocks, and one global contrast mode. At the candidate root the global mode is zero; the strict determinant estimate using concavity of a^(log2 3)−a²/2−1 on [2,4] keeps all standard blocks negative. The root is unique in (1,2) and monotonic. Schoenberg equivalence gives all-scale positivity, and the small-scale expansion gives failure above the root. Centered rank is N−2 at the unique threshold. Independent graph-BFS and quadratic-form checker passed 26,836 finite assertions, supporting but not replacing the all-parameter argument.

originality.rationale: Bounded search of exact graph families, positive definite exponential distance-power kernels, p-negative type and generalized roundness, and broader spectral corona theorems found no source establishing the all-parameter sharp threshold, global-sector dominance, endpoint nullity, strict two-variable monotonicity, or the two asymptotic laws. Sánchez 2011 covers general finite-metric methods and complete bipartite graphs; Indulal–Stevanović 2015 treats only unpowered distance spectra. A same-graph general-position polynomial concerns a different invariant. Historic priority is not certified; a less-indexed equivalent treatment remains possible.

value.rationale: The exact all-scale Gaussian positivity region is a natural harmonic-kernel property of an infinite two-parameter family of graph metric spaces. The result identifies which of the competing symmetry sectors first loses conditional negative type, gives exact one-mode critical degeneration, strict graph-parameter comparison, and two distinct large-parameter expansions. None is an arbitrary finite table entry, and the nontrivial mode-dominance inequality is needed beyond a standard p=1 graph-distance spectrum.
